public_rationale: The ILO's May 20, 2025 report measures potential occupational exposure, not actual job losses [e1]. Challenger's January 8, 2026 report counts 54,836 AI-cited job cuts announced by U.S.-based employers during 2025, not completed global replacements [e2]. NBER's May 2026 summary covers firm surveys conducted in four countries between November 2025 and January 2026 and reports small employment effects [e3]. These sources provide neither a representative estimate nor a credible bound for the share of the global starting workforce actually replaced by AI during 2025, leaving the thresholds unsettled [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Exposure, announced cuts and firm employment effects do not measure realized gross worker replacement [e1, e2, e3].
The evidence lacks a global replacement count and matching beginning-of-2025 workforce denominator [e1, e2, e3].
A single annual replacement rate would not establish the calibration of the probabilistic expectation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: By end of 2025 less than 10%, probably less than 5%, of the workforce will be replaced by AI.

statement.excerpt: Less than 10% of the work force will be replaced by AI. Probably less than 5%.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: Less than 10% of the work force
our_interpretation: The post frames the forecast as replacement during calendar 2025.
With no country specified, workforce is read globally. The denominator is people employed at the beginning of 2025.
Replaced means a worker's job is eliminated because AI takes over the work. Task changes, exposure to automation, and announced plans are not realized replacement.
The firm threshold is below 10%. Below 5% is a secondary, explicitly probabilistic expectation.
Net employment growth cannot by itself establish low replacement, because new jobs can offset displaced jobs.
criteria.support_condition: A representative estimate or credible upper bound places actual AI replacement during 2025 below 10% of the starting workforce. An estimate below 5% also aligns with the secondary expectation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A representative estimate or credible lower bound establishes replacement of at least 10% during 2025. A result between 5% and 10% supports the firm threshold while missing the secondary expectation.

The summary describes surveys conducted from November 2025 through January 2026 in four countries, with most executives reporting no employment effect. Firm responses over three years do not measure the global share of workers replaced during 2025.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative estimate or credible bound for realized gross AI-attributable worker replacement during calendar 2025, divided by global employment at the beginning of 2025. Uncertainty must distinguish the firm 10% threshold; greater precision could also establish whether replacement was below 5%.
